mainTopic: How a ברייתא about a brother born after יבום or מאמר shows the limits of רבי שמעון's view, plus the dispute over מאמר done against the woman's will
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about brothers, יבום, and a new brother born along the way. It proves from the ברייתא's wording that רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי מאיר only when the יבום happened before the new brother was born, just as רב פפא said. The גמרא then explains a line about a brother who 'did not manage' to do מאמר. It means he did מאמר against the woman's will, which counts for nothing according to the חכמים, who disagree with רבי. רבי learns מאמר from the act of יבום, which works even against her will. The חכמים learn it from ordinary קידושין, which need her consent. Next the גמרא pins down that רבי שמעון's view in the מאמר case applies only when the מאמר came before the birth. It also explains why חליצה with the woman who received מאמר cannot free her צרה: a doubt cannot remove a certainty. Finally, רב מנשה בר זביד's question turns out to be about the רבנן's reason. They learn from a פסוק that the first levirate bond stays on her. The amud ends as the גמרא starts a challenge to that from a משנה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון on ביאה, חליצה, and the woman who received מאמר
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that ביאה or חליצה with one of the women exempts her צרה. But חליצה with the woman who only received מאמר does not exempt the צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: ביאה or חליצה with one of them exempts her צרה. If he did חליצה with the woman who received מאמר, the צרה is not exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא, and רבי שמעון gives his ruling on the case where the brother had only done מאמר (a first-stage levirate betrothal) before he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Full ביאה or חליצה with one of the women releases her צרה too. But חליצה with the woman who only received מאמר does not release the צרה. A מאמר may not be as strong as a full marriage, so it may not fully tie the two women together.

keyTerms.meaning: Intercourse, which is how יבום is completed
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
A rival wife, meaning a co-wife of the same husband
A rabbinic first-stage betrothal of the יבמה, done with money or a document
Exempts or releases

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Intercourse or chalitza
with one of them
phrases.notes: Here "one of them" means the second brother's own wife, the one who is not the woman who received מאמר.

phrases.english: exempts her rival wife;
if he performed chalitza with the one who received ma'amar,
the rival wife is not exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: בִּיאָתָהּ אוֹ חֲלִיצָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that was brought earlier in the daf to support רב פפא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Full ביאה or חליצה with one woman exempts her צרה, but חליצה with the woman who received מאמר does not.

steps.title: Cases where both women are fully exempt
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the brother married the יבמה and died before the new brother was born. Or suppose the new brother was born before the יבום. In both cases the two women are exempt from both חליצה and יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he married her and died, and afterward a brother was born; or a brother was born and afterward he married her and died, both women are exempt from חליצה and from יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists two cases where no one argues: the women are completely free, with no יבום and no חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both orders, the new brother was never alive together with the first brother who died. That makes the first widow אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, a wife the new brother may never marry. Her צרה is also exempt because she is that woman's rival wife.

keyTerms.meaning: He married her through יבום
A brother was born to him
Exempt (said of the women)
Levirate marriage

phrases.english: If he married her and died,
and afterward a brother was born to him,
or if a brother was born to him
and afterward he married her, and died,
both of them are exempt
from chalitza and from yibum.

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the order of events straight. Here the new brother is born either after the יבום brother died, or before the יבום happened. The case the תנאים argue about comes next.
steps.triggerLanguage: כְּנָסָהּ וָמֵת, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹלַד לוֹ אָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the מאמר case to the case of a full marriage
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Born after the death, or born before the יבום: both women are exempt from חליצה and יבום.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון argue when the brother is born after the יבום
steps.stepSummary: The case is יבום first, then the new brother is born, then the יבום brother dies. רבי מאיר says both women are exempt. רבי שמעון says the new brother may do יבום or חליצה with whichever woman he chooses.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he married her, then a brother was born, and afterward he died, both are exempt, says רבי מאיר. רבי שמעון says: since the new brother came and found her permitted, and she was never forbidden to him even for a moment, he may do יבום or חליצה with whichever one he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the case that is argued about: the יבום happened first, and only then was the new brother born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, she still counts as the wife of a brother who was never alive together with the new brother, so she stays forbidden. רבי שמעון says otherwise. When the new brother was born, she was already the living second brother's wife, so she was never forbidden to him as a יבמה from the first brother.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, or because
In a permitted state
In a forbidden state

phrases.english: If he married her and a brother was born to him,
and afterward he died,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּיהֶן פְּטוּרוֹת מִן הַחֲלִיצָה וּמִן הַיִּיבּוּם,
phrases.english: both of them are exempt from chalitza and from yibum;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And Rabbi Shimon says:
Since he came and found her in a permitted state,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עָמְדָה עָלָיו שָׁעָה אַחַת בְּאִיסּוּר
phrases.english: and she never stood forbidden to him for even one moment,
he performs yibum with whichever of them he wants,
or performs chalitza with whichever of them he wants.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the מחלוקת that the rest of the section analyzes. The question is whether רבי שמעון also disagrees in the other order of events.
steps.triggerLanguage: כְּנָסָהּ וְנוֹלַד לוֹ אָח, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third order of events, and this time there is a מחלוקת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: both exempt. רבי שמעון: since she was never forbidden to him, he may do יבום or חליצה with either woman.

steps.title: Who was the last section written for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the last case of the ברייתא was meant to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: This last section: for whom is it taught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting and asks a question about how the ברייתא is built. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists "born after יבום" as its own separate case. The גמרא wants to know whose opinion needed that separate listing.

keyTerms.meaning: A section or clause of a source
The last part of a source
For whom is it taught?

phrases.english: This section of the latter clause,
for whom is it taught?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא בָּבָא דְסֵיפָא לְמַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes how the ברייתא just quoted is built
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose opinion was the separate "born after יבום" case written to explain?

steps.title: It cannot be for רבי מאיר, who treats both orders the same
steps.stepSummary: For רבי מאיר, the order of יבום and birth makes no difference. So if the case were written for him, the ברייתא should have combined the cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is taught for רבי מאיר: after all, רבי מאיר sees no difference between יבום and then birth, or birth and then יבום. So let the ברייתא combine them and teach them together!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible answer, רבי מאיר, and shows that it does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר makes both women exempt in every order of events. If the ברייתא were only giving his view, splitting the cases into separate sections would be pointless. One combined line would have been enough.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, which tests a possible answer
After all, or since
It makes no difference to him
Let it combine them and teach them together

phrases.english: If you say it is taught for Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדִי לָא שָׁנֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: but after all, it makes no difference to Rabbi Meir
whether he did yibum and afterward the brother was born
or the brother was born and afterward he did yibum!
Let it combine them and teach them together!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the separate last section was written for רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי מאיר the order of events doesn't matter, so separate sections would be pointless. They should have been combined.

steps.title: So it is for רבי שמעון, who disagrees only when יבום came first
steps.stepSummary: The separate section must be for רבי שמעון. He disagrees only when the יבום came before the birth, and agrees the women are exempt when the birth came first. This supports רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it for רבי שמעון? He disagrees when יבום came first and then the brother was born, but not when the brother was born first and then יבום. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the separate listing was needed for רבי שמעון. That proves where his disagreement stops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of events matters only to רבי שמעון. So the ברייתא split the cases to show that he argues only in the "יבום then birth" case. This confirms רב פפא's claim that רבי שמעון does not disagree when the birth came first.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not, which leads to the right answer
He disagrees
Learn from this, meaning this proves it

phrases.english: Rather, is it not for Rabbi Shimon?
And where he did yibum and afterward the brother was born, he disagrees;

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹלַד וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִיבֵּם — לָא פְּלִיג.
phrases.english: where the brother was born and afterward he did yibum, he does not disagree.
Learn from this.
phrases.notes: This confirms what רב פפא said earlier, that רבי שמעון argues only when the יבום came first.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון permits the new brother only when the יבום happened before he was born. If he was born first, even רבי שמעון agrees both women are exempt.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבי מאיר doesn't fit, the section must be for רבי שמעון
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that רבי שמעון disagrees only when יבום came before the birth
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's separate listing of the "born after יבום" case
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא proves that רבי שמעון's disagreement is limited to the case of יבום followed by the birth, just as רב פפא said.

steps.title: Quoting the case of the unfinished מאמר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line of the ברייתא. The second brother set out to do מאמר but did not manage before a new brother was born, and then he died. The first woman is exempt, and the second may do חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: The second brother set out to do מאמר with his יבמה, but did not manage to do it before a new brother was born. Then the second brother died. The first woman goes free, because she was the wife of a brother who never lived at the same time as the newborn. The second woman does either חליצה or יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the ברייתא so it can analyze it. This is setting up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first woman (the widow of the first brother) is fully exempt, because the newborn never lived at the same time as her husband. The second woman (the second brother's own wife) is treated as a normal יבמה for the newborn. That means whatever the second brother 'tried' did not tie her to her co-wife.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic betrothal the יבם gives the יבמה before יבום
His יבמה, his dead brother's widow
The wife of a brother who did not live at the same time as him; she is exempt from יבום and חליצה
She does חליצה
She does יבום

phrases.english: The Master said:
The second brother set out to do מאמר with his יבמה,
but did not manage to do מאמר with his יבמה
before a brother was born to him, and then he died —
the first woman goes free
phrases.notes: The 'first woman' is the widow of the brother who died first. The 'second' is the second brother's own wife.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ,
phrases.english: because she is the wife of a brother who was not in his world,
and the second woman either does חליצה or does יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: עָמַד הַשֵּׁנִי לַעֲשׂוֹת מַאֲמָר בִּיבִמְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with רב פפא's support, the גמרא returns to the ברייתא and quotes another line of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the מאמר was not completed before the new brother's birth, the first woman is exempt and the second may do חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: What do 'set out' and 'did not manage' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording. Either he did מאמר or he didn't, so why talk about 'setting out' and 'not managing'?
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'set out' mean, and what does 'did not manage' mean? If he did it, he did it. If he didn't do it, he didn't do it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's odd wording. Only actions count in הלכה, not plans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he simply never did מאמר, the ברייתא should just say he did nothing. Describing his intention adds nothing. So the words must point to something more specific.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'stood up'; here, 'set out' to do something
Did not manage, did not get to it in time
If he did it, he did it; only the actual action matters

phrases.english: What does "set out" mean,
and what does "did not manage" mean?
If he did it, he did it,
and if he did not do it, he did not do it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״עָמַד״, וּמַאי ״לֹא הִסְפִּיק״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the line just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Intentions have no legal effect, so describing what he set out to do adds nothing. Either the action happened or it didn't.

steps.title: He did מאמר, but against her will
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the words. 'Set out' means he planned to do it with her consent. 'Did not manage' means he did not get her consent and did it against her will. So the ברייתא does not follow רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'set out' means with her consent. 'Did not manage' means he did not manage to do it with her consent, and did it against her will instead. This ברייתא is not like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he really did do מאמר, but without her agreement. The ברייתא treats that as having no effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets the second woman do יבום as if no מאמר happened. So it must hold that מאמר against her will does nothing. That is the view that disagrees with רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: With her consent
Against her will
Not in line with רבי's opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'did not manage' as 'he did nothing.' He did perform מאמר. It just doesn't count, because she did not agree.

phrases.english: Rather: "set out" means with her consent,
and "did not manage" means he did not manage with her consent,
but did it against her will instead,
and this is not like רבי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: ״עָמַד״ — מִדַּעְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words seemed to describe only an intention that never became an action.
steps.terutzMaskana: He did perform מאמר, but against her will, and the ברייתא holds that such a מאמר has no effect.

steps.title: The dispute about מאמר without consent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a ברייתא. If a יבם does מאמר without her consent, רבי says it works and חכמים say it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If someone does מאמר with his יבמה without her consent, רבי says he acquired her, and the חכמים say he did not acquire her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the dispute it just mentioned. This shows that our ברייתא follows חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, a מאמר done against her will takes full effect. According to חכמים, it takes no effect. Our ברייתא, which ignores the forced מאמר, matches חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: He acquired her; the act took effect
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
One who does מאמר with his יבמה without her consent,
רבי says: he acquired her,
and the Sages say: he did not acquire her.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הָעוֹשֶׂה מַאֲמָר בִּיבִמְתּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim that our ברייתא is not like רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: מאמר against her will takes effect. חכמים: it does not.

steps.title: רבי learns from יבום itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי's reason. He compares מאמר to the act of יבום, which works even against her will.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי's reason? He learns from the relations of יבום. Just as יבום through relations works even against her will, so too the betrothal of a יבמה works even against her will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי's reason and answers right away. He compares מאמר to the act of יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, the act of יבום works even without her consent. רבי says מאמר, which is the betrothal part of יבום, follows the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
He learns, he derives by comparison
Marital relations; here, the act that completes יבום
Betrothal

phrases.english: What is רבי's reason?
He learns from the relations of a יבמה:
just as relations with a יבמה work even against her will,
so too betrothal of a יבמה works even against her will.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי's side of the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי's view that a forced מאמר works
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He compares it to the act of יבום, which works against her will.

steps.title: The רבנן learn from regular betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן compare מאמר to ordinary קידושין, which always needs the woman's consent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן learn from regular betrothal. Just as regular betrothal needs her consent, so too the betrothal of a יבמה needs her consent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's source, which is the opposite comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary קידושין never work without the woman's agreement. The רבנן treat מאמר as a kind of קידושין, so it also needs her consent.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, the same as חכמים here
They learn, they derive
Ordinary betrothal, as everyone does it

phrases.english: And the Rabbis learn from regular betrothal:
just as regular betrothal needs her consent,
so too betrothal of a יבמה needs her consent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן גָּמְרִי מִקִּדּוּשִׁין דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing comparison, for the רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן compare מאמר to ordinary קידושין, which require consent.

steps.title: The root of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle they disagree about. רבי says יבום laws should be learned from other יבום laws. The רבנן say betrothal laws should be learned from other betrothal laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they arguing about? One Sage holds that we should learn יבמה matters from other יבמה matters. The other Sage holds that we should learn betrothal matters from other betrothal matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why each side chose its comparison, and gives the basic principle behind each choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מאמר is both part of יבום and a kind of betrothal. רבי puts it in the יבום group, so it follows the rule of the act of יבום. The רבנן put it in the betrothal group, so it follows the rule of ordinary קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?
One Sage holds
Matters, laws
To learn, to derive

steps.whatToRemember: A מאמר done against the יבמה's will works according to רבי, who learns it from the act of יבום. It does not work according to the רבנן, who learn it from ordinary קידושין. Our ברייתא follows the רבנן, which is why 'did not manage' means the forced מאמר did not count.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
One Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This first 'מר' is רבי. The second 'מר' below is the רבנן.

phrases.english: matters of a יבמה from matters of a יבמה
one should learn,
and the other Sage holds:
matters of betrothal from matters of betrothal
one should learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two comparisons to the single principle that explains why each side chose its comparison.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle of the dispute
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whether מאמר is classified with יבום laws or with קידושין laws.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute depends on whether מאמר is learned from יבום (רבי) or from קידושין (רבנן).

steps.title: The ברייתא's case of מאמר and a brother born later
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that the first widow goes free as אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, and the second brother's own wife does חליצה but not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did מאמר with her and afterward a brother was born to him, or a brother was born and afterward he did מאמר, and then he died: the first woman goes free because she is the wife of a brother who never lived at the same time as him. The second woman does חליצה but does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the ברייתא so that it can explain it. This line gives the תנא קמא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'first' woman is the first brother's widow, who got the מאמר. The newborn third brother never lived at the same time as her husband, so she is fully free. The 'second' woman, the second brother's own wife, is tied up with that מאמר widow, so she may only do חליצה and not יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: A יבם's betrothal of his brother's widow with money or a document, done before יבום
The wife of a brother who died before this brother was born. She is never a candidate for יבום with him.
She does חליצה, the ceremony that frees her without יבום
She does יבום (levirate marriage)

steps.confusionAlert: 'First' and 'second' here mean the two women: the first brother's widow and the second brother's wife. They do not mean the order of events.

phrases.english: If he performed levirate betrothal with her
phrases.notes: 'He' is the second brother. 'Her' is the first brother's widow.

phrases.english: and afterward a brother was born to him,
or a brother was born to him

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ עָשָׂה בָּהּ מַאֲמָר, וָמֵת —
phrases.english: and afterward he performed levirate betrothal with her, and he died —
the first woman goes out (is free)

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ,
phrases.english: because she is the wife of his brother who was not in his world,
and the second performs חליצה but does not enter into יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָשָׂה בָּהּ מַאֲמָר וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹלַד לוֹ אָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new section of the ברייתא after the מאמר-without-consent discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first widow goes free as אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו. The second brother's wife does חליצה, not יבום.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: one act frees the other wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that ביאה or חליצה with either woman frees her צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: יבום or חליצה with one of them frees her co-wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי שמעון's opposing view. He treats the two women as a linked pair, so one act takes care of both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא let the first woman go free with no act at all. רבי שמעון holds she still belongs to the יבום situation, so ביאה or חליצה with one of the women frees her צרה. But חליצה with the woman who received the מאמר does not free her צרה, as step 19 shows. This sets up the גמרא's next question: which case does he mean?

keyTerms.meaning: Relations with her, meaning יבום
Her co-wife (another wife of the same husband)
Frees, exempts

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Her intercourse or her חליצה
of one of them
exempts her rival wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to the תנא קמא in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי שמעון, ביאה or חליצה with one of the women frees her צרה, but חליצה with the בעלת מאמר does not free the צרה (step 19).

steps.title: Which case is רבי שמעון talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא listed two orders of events, so the גמרא asks which one רבי שמעון argues on.
steps.simpleTranslation: To which case is רבי שמעון referring?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. It is setting up the next move, where it will test each of the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed two cases: מאמר before the birth, and birth before the מאמר. רבי שמעון's words could fit either one, so the גמרא wants to pin down which.

keyTerms.meaning: On which case is he standing? (Which case does he refer to?)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, on which case does he stand?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַהֵיָיא קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רבי שמעון's statement in step 15 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the two orders of events רבי שמעון argues on.

steps.title: It cannot be the case where the birth came first
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון cannot be arguing where the brother was born before the מאמר, because we already know he agrees in that order.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he refers to the case where a brother was born and afterward he did מאמר, you already said that where the brother was born and only later he did יבום, רבי שמעון does not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option and turns it down. It reminds us of something already established about רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that when the third brother is born first and the יבום comes after, רבי שמעון agrees she is forbidden as אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו. If he agrees even with full יבום in that order, he surely agrees with a mere מאמר. So that cannot be the case he argues on.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (proposes an option that will be rejected)
He does not argue
And only afterward

phrases.english: If we say: on the case where a brother was born to him
and afterward he performed levirate betrothal with her —
didn't you say that where he was born and afterward he did יבום
Rabbi Shimon does not dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא אַנּוֹלַד לוֹ אָח וְאַחַר כָּךְ עָשָׂה בָּהּ מַאֲמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rules out the first possible answer to step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out reading רבי שמעון as arguing on the birth-first case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי שמעון already agrees when the birth comes first, even with full יבום.

steps.title: He argues where the מאמר came first
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון argues only where the מאמר was done before the third brother was born.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he refers to the case where he did מאמר with her and afterward a brother was born.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer. רבי שמעון's argument applies only to the order where the מאמר came first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the birth-first case is ruled out, only the מאמר-first case is left. In that order, the מאמר already tied her to the second brother before the third was born. This is where רבי שמעון says one act frees both women.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (brings the accepted answer after rejecting the first option)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון argues only when the מאמר came before the third brother's birth. When the birth came first, he agrees with the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: Rather, on the case where he performed levirate betrothal with her
and afterward a brother was born to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַעָשָׂה בָּהּ מַאֲמָר וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹלַד לוֹ אָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer that remains after step 17 ruled out the other option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון argues on the case where the מאמר was done before the brother was born.

steps.title: חליצה with the בעלת מאמר does not free the צרה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that if he did חליצה with the woman who got the מאמר, her צרה is not freed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did חליצה with the woman who received the מאמר, the co-wife is not freed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא. It will explain the reason in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually חליצה with one wife frees her co-wife. Here the ברייתא says it does not work when the חליצה is done with the woman who only received a מאמר.

keyTerms.meaning: The woman who received a מאמר
Was freed or exempted

phrases.english: If he performed חליצה with the woman of the levirate betrothal,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the third brother. The בעלת מאמר is the first brother's widow.

phrases.english: the rival wife is not exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָלַץ לְבַעֲלַת מַאֲמָר לֹא נִפְטְרָה צָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a later line of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה with the בעלת מאמר does not free the צרה.

steps.title: A ספק cannot remove a ודאי
steps.stepSummary: The צרה is definitely tied to יבום, while the בעלת מאמר is only possibly tied. A doubtful חליצה cannot free a definite obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the co-wife is definitely bound, and the בעלת מאמר is only possibly bound, and a doubt cannot take something out of a certainty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 19 and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second brother's own wife is definitely bound to יבום. It is unclear whether the מאמר made the first widow truly his wife. So her חליצה might not count at all, and an act that might not count cannot release the wife who is definitely bound.

keyTerms.meaning: Certain, definite
Doubt, uncertain
A doubt cannot remove a certainty

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי comes up all over ש"ס: a doubtful act cannot undo a definite obligation.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the rival wife is a certainty,
and the woman of the levirate betrothal is a doubt,
phrases.notes: It is unclear whether a מאמר really makes her the second brother's wife.

phrases.english: and a doubt does not take out of the hands of a certainty.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא מִשּׁוּם דַּהֲוַאי צָרָה וַדַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ruling of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The צרה is definitely bound and the בעלת מאמר only possibly bound, so her doubtful חליצה cannot free the צרה.

steps.title: רב מנשה בר זביד asks for רבי שמעון's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה בר זביד, sitting before רב הונא, asks what רבי שמעון's reason is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשה בר זביד sat before רב הונא, and he sat and said: What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רב מנשה בר זביד asks for the reason behind רבי שמעון's view, and this sets up the גמרא's surprised reaction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He asks why רבי שמעון lets the third brother do יבום with the widow of a brother he never lived alongside, when the יבום happened before his birth. His question seems strange, as the next step shows.

keyTerms.meaning: Sat
Before him (in front of his teacher)

phrases.english: Rav Menashe bar Zevid sat
before Rav Huna
and he sat and was saying:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב מְנַשֶּׁה בַּר זְבִיד קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי שמעון's view with a new question about his reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind רבי שמעון's view.

steps.title: Why ask? The reason is written in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised at the question, because רבי שמעון's reason is stated right in the ברייתא: he found her permitted, and she was never forbidden to him even for a moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי שמעון's reason?! It is as he himself stated the reason: since he came and found her permitted, and she was never forbidden to him for even one moment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מנשה's question. רבי שמעון already gave his reason, so what is there to ask?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי שמעון explains that when the third brother was born, the woman was already married through יבום and was permitted to him. She was never forbidden to him even for a moment. Since the reason is spelled out, the גמרא wonders what רב מנשה really meant. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Since
In a permitted state
One moment
In a forbidden state

steps.confusionAlert: The repeated words מאי טעמא דרבי שמעון are not a second question. They are the גמרא repeating רב מנשה's words in surprise, as if to say: why ask that?

phrases.english: What is Rabbi Shimon's reason?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is repeating his question in surprise, as if asking why he even needed to ask.

phrases.english: It is as he stated the reason:
Since he came and found her in a permitted state,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עָמְדָה עָלָיו שָׁעָה אַחַת בְּאִיסּוּר!
phrases.english: and she never stood forbidden to him for one moment!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כִּדְאָמַר טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the question asked in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מנשה בר זביד's question about רבי שמעון's reason.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The question seems unnecessary, since רבי שמעון's reason is written in the ברייתא itself: the woman was permitted when the third brother was born and was never forbidden to him.

steps.title: The real question was about the רבנן's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question to רב הונא was really about the reason of the רבנן, not רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question was: what is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem from the last step by explaining what the question really was. It was asking about the רבנן, and this sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22 the גמרא said that רבי שמעון's reason is written right in the ברייתא, so nobody would need to ask about it. So the question must have been the opposite one. Since רבי שמעון's logic ('he found her permitted') sounds so convincing, why do the רבנן still forbid her?

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a corrected version of what was said
The reason of the Sages (the majority opinion)
The Sages who disagree with רבי שמעון

phrases.english: Rather: what is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the surprise of step 22 by reinterpreting the question of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the question being asked
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב מנשה בר זביד was asking for רבי שמעון's reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was asking for the reason of the רבנן, since רבי שמעון's reason is obvious and strong.

steps.title: The verse shows the first levirate bond remains
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn from 'וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה וְיִבְּמָהּ' that the first levirate bond is still on her even after she is taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he shall take her to him as a wife and do יבום with her.' This means the first levirate bond is still on her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving the רבנן's source from a פסוק. Even after the brother takes her, her first levirate status has not gone away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first says 'he shall take her as a wife' and only afterward says 'וְיִבְּמָהּ', calling it יבום. So even once she is taken, she is still seen as a יבמה connected to her first husband. That is why, for the רבנן, she still counts as the wife of the first brother, whom the new brother never lived alongside, and she stays forbidden to him.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall do יבום with her
The first levirate bond, which comes from her first husband's death

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core of the מחלוקת. רבי שמעון holds that once she was taken in יבום before the new brother was born, she was permitted to him and the old bond no longer counts against her. The רבנן hold that the old bond stays on her.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And he shall take her to him as a wife and perform levirate marriage with her,'
the first levirate bond is still upon her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reframed question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the פסוק 'וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה וְיִבְּמָהּ': the first levirate bond remains on her even after she is taken.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה that she is like his wife in every way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge the רבנן using a משנה that says once he takes her, she is fully his wife, and starts quoting רבי יוסי בר חנינא's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the משנה that teaches: if he took her, she is like his wife in every way? And רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: this teaches...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to the answer it just gave. It quotes a משנה and starts quoting רבי יוסי בר חנינא's teaching on it, and that teaching finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that once the brother takes the יבמה, she is 'like his wife in every way.' That seems to clash with the idea that the first levirate bond is still on her. The full force of the challenge depends on what רבי יוסי בר חנינא learns from this משנה, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: That which we learned in a משנה
He took her (married the יבמה through יבום)
Like his wife in every way
It teaches; introduces what we learn from a source

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not finished here. רבי יוסי בר חנינא's teaching is only beginning, so wait for the next amud before deciding what the problem is.

phrases.english: But that which we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: This משנה appears later in the מסכתא, on דף ל״ח.

phrases.aramaic: כְּנָסָהּ — הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאִשְׁתּוֹ לְכׇל דָּבָר.
phrases.english: If he took her, she is like his wife in every respect.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: מְלַמֵּד
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: This teaches
phrases.notes: His sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 24 by quoting a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the first levirate bond remains on her after she is taken
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says that once he takes her she is like his wife in every respect. That suggests the old levirate bond is gone, and רבי יוסי בר חנינא's teaching will spell out how.
